extracted.intended_audience: patent and design litigators, solicitors, and registrants working under the UK Designs & Patents framework (1883)
extracted.subtask_description: Forms, procedural requirements, and substantive objections/grounds used in patent, design (copyright) and trade mark litigation under the 1883 Act; includes trademark goods classification and model pleadings, motions and orders (injunctions, inspection, accounts, petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Claim — Patent infringement (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Statement of Claim in an action for infringement of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify the defendant's infringement of the plaintiff's Patent No., grant term and grant date, state plaintiff was first inventor, claim injunction to restrain further infringement and a sum for damages, deliver particulars of breaches, and specify place of trial. (Form based on Rules of the Supreme Court, 1883.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars and Notice of Breaches (attachment to claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details to accompany Statement of Claim setting out particulars and notice of breaches as required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should state that defendants have at divers times between certain dates infringed the patent by manufacture, sale, or use or imitation of the invention/ specification; if precise days/amounts unknown, advise plaintiffs will claim full compensation when ascertained and may claim an account and payment of all profits and an injunction against repetition and continuance of infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Defence — Patent infringement (form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Statement of Defence in an action for infringement of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated defences: 1) did not infringe; 2) invention not new; 3) plaintiff not first inventor; 4) invention not useful; 5) denial of other factual matters affecting validity; 6) patent not assigned to plaintiff. Delivered and signed with date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars and Notice of Objections (attachment to defence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars of objections the defendant will rely on at trial, delivered with the Statement of Defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated objections include: no infringement; plaintiff not first inventor; invention not new; not proper subject of letters patent; patent for a principle only (not a manner of new manufacture); claim is a principle of applying old contrivances to new objects; invention not useful; specification fails to describe/ascertain nature or manner of performance; invention does not produce described effects; specification not enabling to a person of reasonable skill; some alternative methods described are impracticable; omission of necessary steps/processes; specification fails to distinguish claimed from admitted-old matters; invention generally known prior to grant; prior use; prior publication in UK; prior manufacture and sale by others. The form may cite specific publications, dates, and reliance upon whole specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Motion to Restrain Infringement (interim relief motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form of notice for moving the court for an interim injunction to restrain infringement pending trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must state the court, date and time, parties bringing the motion, and the precise relief sought: restraining defendant and associated persons from making/selling any article made according to the patented process or any colourable imitation until trial or further order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory Order Granting Injunction to an Assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: Court order granting an interlocutory injunction in favour of an assignee of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically granted with the usual undertaking as to damages; restrains defendants, servants, etc., from making, using or practising the invention as described in specification and drawings until trial or further order. May include express carve-outs (e.g., skates made by plaintiff/agent). Citation: Seton, i. p. 344.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory Order Refusing Injunction; Undertaking to Keep Account
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may refuse an interlocutory injunction but require defendant to keep an account of monies received from the alleged infringing subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if defendant undertakes to keep account of moneys received from sale/use of the accused article, court may refuse injunction and order motion costs to be costs in the cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Motion to Inspect Defendant's Machine (discovery by inspection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion requesting the court to order inspection of defendant's machines/processes in a patent action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed order may require defendant to file an affidavit verifying kinds of machines sold/exposed for sale since a stated date; to produce one of each different kind for inspection at solicitor's office; permit plaintiff, solicitors, agent, and three named scientific witnesses to inspect and work the machines upon three days' prior written notice; production for examination and trial; costs may be ordered in the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for Inspection by Experts and to Take Samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Order permitting named experts to enter defendant's premises to inspect manufacturing processes and take samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts (named A. and B.) may, on three days' notice, inspect the process, examine whole process of manufacture as alleged, take samples upon paying reasonable charges, and make observations necessary to obtain full information and evidence of mode of manufacture (Seton, i. p. 350).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction after Trial — Account of Sales and Profits; Delivery Up
rubrics_metrics.description: Final injunction following trial with ancillary relief: account of sales and profits, discovery, and delivery up or destruction of infringing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order restrains defendant and agents during continuance of letters patent from using/exercising the invention or selling articles differing only colourably or by mere mechanical equivalents; directs an account of infringing articles sold and of gains and profits; requires defendant to pay amounts within specified days (e.g., seven days) after certificate and to deliver up, break up or render unfit for use the infringing articles in possession; defendant to pay costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of Intended Application for Prolongation (notice requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required public advertisement of intention to apply for prolongation of patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice: must state intention to present petition to Her Majesty in Council for prolongation and fix/apply for hearing date; any person desirous of opposing must enter caveat at Privy Council Office by a stated deadline. Example timeframe given with solicitor's details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Privy Council for Prolongation — formal and substantive requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Model petition to the Privy Council seeking prolongation (extension) of patent term and the substantive matters to be alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required allegations and supporting matters include: identification of original letters patent (date, grant), filing of full specification and payment of required fees, statement that invention was new at grant date and petitioner was true first inventor, description of invention and reference to specification/models, history of prior related inventions and improvements, evidence of efforts and expenses to introduce invention commercially (manufacture, advertising, agents), readiness to supply articles on fair terms and to grant licences, statement that validity has not been disputed, mention of any foreign patents and their terms, evidence of insufficient profit or failure to obtain remuneration and accounts supporting this, grounds for believing extension would allow petitioner to obtain fair reward and benefit public, compliance with statutory advertisement requirements, and a prayer for prolongation for a further term (e.g., 14 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Claim — Infringement of Copyright in a Registered Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Statement of Claim in action for infringement of copyright in a registered design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must identify the registered design number and class and date of registration; describe the registered design; allege that the prescribed mark was duly placed on all articles to which the design was applied before delivery on sale; set out the acts complained of (with reference to statutory provision, e.g., s.59); claim injunction to restrain defendant and specify any particular injunction sought; claim damages (amount).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Defence — Infringement of Copyright in a Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Statement of Defence in action for infringement of copyright in a registered design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated defences: 1) defendant did not infringe; 2) alleged design not duly registered; 3) copyright had expired prior to the alleged acts; 4) plaintiff did not cause articles to be marked with prescribed mark before delivery on sale nor take proper steps to ensure marking; other particulars as required. Form modeled on trade mark forms (R.S.C. 1883).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunction restraining infringement of copyright in a design
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim or final injunction to restrain infringement of a registered design (copyright in design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically granted with the usual undertaking as to damages; restrains defendant, servants, etc., from selling the design or applying the same or any colourable imitation to any substance or article of manufacture; may specify particular goods (e.g., ornamental sweetmeats) and prohibit manufacturing, offering, exposing for sale, and selling such articles or close imitations (Seton, i. p. 246).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order Continuing Injunction; Delivery Up of Articles; Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Order continuing an injunction against sale/ disposal of articles bearing the plaintiff's design or fraudulent imitations, and ordering delivery up of specified articles and payment of costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: continuation of injunction until a named date and ordering delivery up of articles to which design was applied or fraudulent imitations were applied; case citation McEea v. Holdsworth, 2 De G. & S. 499.
